tool_args.rationale: Fresh confirmation rejected the previous barrier-modulated form, but paid rows remain smooth and stationary rather than chaotic. The archived two-layer sink-inhibited siphon with a positive square-root open branch explains the qualitative pattern: low gradients elevate output, near-unity gradients yield concave saturation, and high gradients suppress it. Fit its three identifiable parameters numerically to all observations; no additional probe is needed.

considered_alternatives.rejected_reason: Already acquired; paired low/high-gradient rows establish a strong gradient effect and positive open-branch response.
The observations are all at H=0.6, but the marked failure is across gradient/substrate response rather than evidence of unresolved time dynamics; a siphon mechanism can be fitted directly.
Its four-parameter barrier activation model was just refuted on fresh confirmation, so use the simpler archived saturating siphon with positive square-root branch.
No observation exceeds the cited supercritical threshold range; the highest gradient is 2.35, below the stated trigger.
